newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile stocks close higher on U.S. buy orders.
newsitem.headline: Chile stocks close higher on U.S. buy orders.

text.p: Chilean stocks closed higher on Tuesday after a wave of U.S. buy orders for electrical sector ADRs as Wall Street reopened after a long holiday weekend, traders said.
The IPSA index of the 40 most-traded shares ended 0.74 percent higher at 126.26 points, while the general IGPA index finished 0.48 percent higher at 5,521.0 points.
The main reason for the rise was Endesa and Enersis, two electricity stocks, a trader said.
Market turnover returned to normal after Monday's lull, totaling 15.8 billion pesos.
Endesa rose 5.75 percent, while Enersis rose 1.25 percent.
Commodity stocks, such as paper pulp and oil producer Copec, and steelmaker CAP, also contributed to the market's rise, a trader said.
He said the prospects for the Wednesday session in Santiago hinged on the strength of U.S. buy orders. Another trader said Chilean stocks should perform strongly for the rest of the week.
Other factors bouying the market were another strong performance by U.S. stocks on Wall Street and continuing speculation that Chile's central bank will cut interest rates.
The biggest declines were by Forestal, which lost 4.35 percent, and Cruzsalud, down 4.0 percent.
The IPSA index of the 40 most-traded shares ended Monday at 125.34 points, 0.09 percent higher than Friday's close, and the general IGPA index ended at 5495.26 points, up 0.06 percent.
